title: Everyone Under a Manager
description: List all the direct and indirect reports of one manager with a recursive CTE.
statement: Return the `employee` name of everyone who reports to **Omar Haddad** (employee id 2), directly or through other managers, at any depth. Omar himself is not included. Order by `employee`.
starter:
SELECT name AS employee
FROM employees;
hints: Start from the direct reports, then keep adding the reports of people you have already found.
`WITH RECURSIVE under_omar(id) AS (SELECT id ... WHERE manager_id = 2 UNION ALL SELECT e.id ... JOIN under_omar ON e.manager_id = under_omar.id)`.
Join the result back to `employees` to get the names. Omar is the starting point, not a member.
solution:
WITH RECURSIVE under_omar(id) AS (
  SELECT id FROM employees WHERE manager_id = 2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id
  FROM employees AS e
  JOIN under_omar ON e.manager_id = under_omar.id
)
SELECT e.name AS employee
FROM employees AS e
JOIN under_omar ON under_omar.id = e.id
ORDER BY e.name;
explanation:
**The idea.** Start with the people whose `manager_id` is Omar's id (the anchor), then repeatedly add the people whose manager is already in the set. When a round adds nobody the recursion stops, and what has been collected is everyone below Omar, however deep.

**Why only the ids.** The recursive part only needs to follow the `manager_id` links, so it carries just `id`; the names come from joining `employees` once at the end.

**Related.** The same query with `WHERE manager_id IS NULL` and a depth column is the org chart; with `parent_id` it is every descendant category; going the other way (from a person up to the top) lists a chain of command.
